name: ServiceNow
one_liner: No central OAuth app or review exists: every customer's ServiceNow admin must register your client on their own instance, so production readiness is a per-customer onboarding task, not an approval.
difficulty_reason: There is no provider review to pass, but there is also no global OAuth app, so every customer instance needs an admin (oauth_admin or admin role) to create an inbound integration and hand you a client ID and secret before any end user can connect.
time_to_first_test: 20-40 minutes on a ServiceNow instance you already have admin access to (inferred; not published)
time_to_production: No provider review; each customer goes live as soon as their admin registers your client (inferred: hours to a few weeks per customer, driven by the customer's own change process). Optional ServiceNow Store certification typically 3-5 weeks.

approval.required_for: Nothing for API access via OAuth. Each customer instance admin must create an inbound OAuth integration for your app. Only a ServiceNow Store listing (optional) requires certification.
approval.who_reviews: The customer's own ServiceNow administrator (per instance). ServiceNow's certification team only if you choose to list on the ServiceNow Store.
approval.typical_wait: No provider wait for OAuth access. Store certification: ServiceNow states it 'typically requires 3-5 weeks'. Per-customer admin turnaround: not published.
approval.cost: Free for OAuth registration on a customer instance. Store listing requires Build Partner / Partner Program membership; fee not confirmed from an official source.

account_prerequisites: A ServiceNow instance where you have admin rights, for building and testing (for example a personal developer instance; availability not checked in this pass)
For each customer: a person on their instance with the oauth_admin, mi_admin, or admin role (Machine Identity Console flow) or oauth_admin (old Application Registry flow)
A stable HTTPS redirect (callback) URL for your app, or the Composio redirect URI if you use Composio
Optional: a logo URL to show on the instance's consent (Allow/Deny) page
Optional: ServiceNow Build Partner / Partner Program membership, only if you want a ServiceNow Store listing

steps.title: Decide the grant type
steps.detail: Use the authorization code grant so each end user signs in to their own instance and actions run as that user (respects their ACLs). Use client credentials only for a service-account style integration where actions are attributed to one integration user; it is off by default and needs extra admin setup. Avoid ROPC (password) grant.

steps.title: Build and test against your own instance
steps.detail: On an instance you control, create an inbound integration (see next step), then test the flow: https://<instance>.service-now.com/oauth_auth.do?response_type=code&client_id=...&redirect_uri=... and exchange the code at https://<instance>.service-now.com/oauth_token.do.

steps.title: Write a customer admin setup guide (current UI)
steps.detail: Instruct the customer admin: Machine Identity Console > Inbound integrations > New integration > OAuth - Authorization code grant. Fill Name, Provider name (mandatory), Redirect URL (your callback exactly), leave Client Secret blank to auto-generate or paste one, keep Active checked, optionally add an auth scope and Logo URL, and leave token lifespans at default unless agreed (access 1800 s, refresh 8,640,000 s = 100 days). Save, then send you the Client ID, Client Secret, and instance URL over a secure channel.

steps.title: Include the legacy path for older instances
steps.detail: On instances without the Machine Identity Console flow: All > System OAuth > Application Registry > New > 'Create an OAuth API endpoint for external clients'. Same fields (Name, Client Secret, Redirect URL, Refresh/Access Token Lifespan, Active).

steps.title: Store credentials per instance
steps.detail: Model each customer as its own OAuth client: store instance base URL + client ID + client secret per tenant. Build auth and token URLs from the instance URL (or the customer's custom instance URL). In Composio, this means one custom auth config per customer instance (inferred).

steps.title: Handle token refresh and expiry
steps.detail: Refresh access tokens before 30 minutes. Plan for refresh tokens expiring after 100 days by default (or whatever the admin set); when it expires the user must re-consent.

steps.title: (Optional) Client credentials for machine integrations
steps.detail: If a customer prefers no per-user login: admin creates system property glide.oauth.inbound.client.credential.grant_type.enabled = true and sets the OAuth Application User on the OAuth entity (or uses Machine Identity Console > Client Credentials Grant). All actions then run as that user.

steps.title: (Optional) Evaluate CIMD for newer instances
steps.detail: On Zurich Patch 7+ or Australia Patch 1+, a public client with PKCE can be identified by an HTTPS Client ID Metadata Document URL instead of a secret. The admin still must register your CIMD client on each instance, but no secret exchange is needed.

steps.title: (Optional) ServiceNow Store listing
steps.detail: Only if you want a scoped app on the ServiceNow Store (for example to ship setup automation). Requires Build Partner membership and certification. Not needed for OAuth API access.

nuances: Every URL is instance-specific: https://<instance>.service-now.com/oauth_auth.do and /oauth_token.do. There is no global login.servicenow.com authorization server for API access.
Redirect URL matching: the old Application Registry form says 'If no match is made, the instance uses the first redirect URL.' Register your exact callback first.
Default token lifespans: access token 1800 seconds (30 minutes), refresh token 8,640,000 seconds (100 days). Admins can change both per client, so do not hardcode.
The user sees an Allow/Deny approval page on their instance; if the instance uses SSO, the user is redirected to the customer IdP first.
Access follows the signed-in user's roles and ACLs for authorization code; for client credentials it follows the configured OAuth Application User.
Client credentials grant is disabled by default ('By default the system property is false').

Enforce token restriction / API access policies can limit which REST APIs your token may call. If tool calls return 401/403 despite a valid token, ask the admin about API access policies and auth scopes.
Auth scopes in the new Machine Identity Console flow can restrict the client to selected APIs; 'useraccount' style broad access depends on admin choices.
Tokens can be JWT or Opaque; JWKS is at api/now/oauth/jwks on the instance.
CIMD replaces Dynamic Client Registration as ServiceNow's supported approach for unregistered clients, but an admin still registers each CIMD client per instance.
Docs now show release 'Brazil' (updated 10 Sep 2026); the Application Registry flow is filed under 'Old Inbound integrations experience'.

blockers.blocker: No central OAuth app: you cannot let any ServiceNow user self-connect without their admin first registering your client.
blockers.how_to_proceed: Make admin setup part of customer onboarding. Ship a one-page admin guide with exact field values and a secure way to submit client ID, secret, and instance URL.

blockers.blocker: Customer admins may refuse to grant broad access or may enable token restrictions that block some APIs.
blockers.how_to_proceed: List the exact REST APIs and tables your agent needs, and suggest an auth scope plus API access policy that covers only those.

blockers.blocker: Composio-managed OAuth is not available for ServiceNow.
blockers.how_to_proceed: Create a custom auth config per customer instance with that instance's client ID and secret, and register Composio's redirect URI in the customer's inbound integration.

blockers.blocker: Refresh tokens expire (100 days by default), forcing users to reconnect.
blockers.how_to_proceed: Detect invalid_grant on refresh and prompt a reconnect, or ask the admin to set a longer refresh token lifespan.

agent_can_do: Draft the customer admin setup guide with exact navigation paths for both the Machine Identity Console flow and the old Application Registry flow
Generate the redirect URI and pre-fill recommended field values (name, provider name, logo URL, token lifespans)
Build per-instance authorization and token URLs from a customer's instance URL
List the ServiceNow REST APIs and tables the agent's tools need, and draft a matching auth scope / API access policy request
Write token refresh and reconnect handling, including invalid_grant detection
Test the OAuth flow end to end on a developer instance you already have access to
you_must_do: Get each customer's ServiceNow admin to create the inbound integration on their instance (only someone with oauth_admin/admin on that instance can do it)
Receive and securely store each customer's client ID and client secret
Agree with each customer's security team on grant type, scopes, and token lifespans
Join the ServiceNow partner program and pass certification only if you choose to list on the ServiceNow Store
composio_note: Composio's ServiceNow toolkit page shows 'Composio-managed OAuth not available'. Supported auth schemes listed are OAuth2, BASIC, and S2S_OAUTH2 (171 tools, version 20260924_00). So you must bring your own OAuth client: for ServiceNow that means each customer's admin creates an inbound integration on their instance with the redirect URI shown in your Composio auth config, and you create a custom auth config with that client ID and secret. Composio's custom-auth docs note that 'Self-hosted or regional variants ... need their own OAuth app', which matches ServiceNow's per-instance model. S2S_OAUTH2 likely maps to client credentials (inferred), which also needs the customer admin to enable the grant.

Authorization and token endpoints are per instance: /oauth_auth.do and /oauth_token.do
Default access token lifespan 1800 seconds; default refresh token lifespan 8,640,000 seconds (100 days); both configurable per client
Client credentials grant is off by default and needs a system property plus an OAuth Application User
Users see an Allow/Deny prompt during authorization code flow
CIMD available from Zurich Patch 7 and Australia Patch 1; still requires per-instance client registration; public clients with PKCE only

The old docs' instruction to append /oauth_redirect.do to the redirect URL describes ServiceNow-as-client callbacks; an external app should register its own exact callback URL (the new form just says 'URL to which the authorization code should be sent')

corrections: Common advice says to use System OAuth > Application Registry > 'Create an OAuth API endpoint for external clients'. Current docs (Brazil, Sep 2026) file this under 'Old Inbound integrations experience'; the primary path is now Machine Identity Console > Inbound integrations > New integration.
Client credentials is often described as simply available; ServiceNow docs say it is disabled by default and needs the glide.oauth.inbound.client.credential.grant_type.enabled property set to true.

CIMD is sometimes read as removing per-instance setup. ServiceNow docs say an instance 'doesn't accept clients on its own' and each CIMD client must be registered; it only removes the client secret exchange.

ServiceNow Store certification is often assumed to be required for an integration. It is only needed to list a scoped app on the Store, not to call ServiceNow APIs with OAuth (inferred from the OAuth docs).
Evidence check 2026-10-28: one source line was a paraphrase, not the docs' wording. Replaced with the exact sentence from the ServiceNow authorization code flow page.
